name: Work and Daily Routines
description: Learn practical words and phrases for workdays, schedules, and regular home activities.

cards.front: What does “schedule” mean in “My schedule is busy on Thursday”?
cards.answer: A plan that shows when activities or tasks will happen.
cards.explanation: A schedule organizes events, work, or appointments by time.
cards.example: I checked my schedule before accepting the meeting.

cards.front: What does “shift” mean in “My shift starts at eight”?
cards.answer: A scheduled period of work.
cards.explanation: A work shift has a set starting time and finishing time.
cards.example: Rosa works the morning shift this week.

cards.front: What does “commute” mean in “He commutes by train”?
cards.answer: Travel regularly between your home and workplace or school.
cards.explanation: To “commute” is to make the regular journey to and from a workplace or school.
cards.example: I commute to the office three days a week.

cards.front: What is a “deadline” in “The deadline is Friday afternoon”?
cards.answer: The latest time when something must be finished.
cards.explanation: A deadline sets the final date or time for completing a task.
cards.example: We finished the project two days before the deadline.

cards.front: What does “task” mean in “This is my first task today”?
cards.answer: A piece of work that needs to be done.
cards.explanation: A task is a specific job or activity, often one part of a larger project.
cards.example: Updating the contact list was a quick task.

cards.front: Who is a “colleague” in “I asked a colleague for help”?
cards.answer: A person you work with.
cards.explanation: A colleague works in the same organization or profession as you.
cards.example: My colleagues shared their ideas during lunch.

cards.front: What is a “meeting” in “We have a team meeting at two”?
cards.answer: A planned time when people come together to discuss something.
cards.explanation: A meeting brings people together in person or online for a shared purpose.
cards.example: The meeting ended after we agreed on the next steps.

cards.front: What does “break” mean in “Let’s take a short break”?
cards.answer: A short period of rest between activities.
cards.explanation: A break is time when you pause work or another activity before continuing.
cards.example: I went outside during my afternoon break.

cards.front: What does “wake up” mean in “I wake up at seven”?
cards.answer: Become awake after sleeping.
cards.explanation: “Wake up” describes the change from sleeping to being awake.
cards.example: She woke up before her alarm rang.

cards.front: What does “get dressed” mean in “I get dressed after breakfast”?
cards.answer: Put on clothes.
cards.explanation: To “get dressed” is to put on the clothes you plan to wear.
cards.example: The children got dressed for school.

cards.front: What does “have breakfast” mean in “We have breakfast at home”?
cards.answer: Eat the first meal of the day.
cards.explanation: “Have breakfast” is a common way to say that someone eats their morning meal.
cards.example: I had breakfast before the early meeting.

cards.front: What does “leave for work” mean in “They leave for work at 8:30”?
cards.answer: Depart in order to go to your workplace.
cards.explanation: To “leave for work” is to depart from where you are in order to go to work.
cards.example: Nora leaves for work just after breakfast.

cards.front: What does “check email” mean in “I check my email after I arrive”?
cards.answer: Open and review email messages.
cards.explanation: To “check email” is to look for and read new or important messages.
cards.example: He checked his email before the first call.

cards.front: What does “start work” mean in “I start work at nine”?
cards.answer: Begin doing your job for the day.
cards.explanation: To “start work” means to begin your work activities.
cards.example: We started work as soon as the equipment arrived.

cards.front: What does “take notes” mean in “Please take notes during the call”?
cards.answer: Write down important information.
cards.explanation: To “take notes” is to record key details so you can remember or use them later.
cards.example: I took notes while the trainer explained the process.

cards.front: What does “finish work” mean in “She finishes work at five”?
cards.answer: Stop doing your job for the day.
cards.explanation: To “finish work” means to complete or stop your work activities at the end of a work period.
cards.example: I finished work early and went for a walk.

cards.front: What does “submit a report” mean in “I need to submit the report today”?
cards.answer: Send or give a completed report to the person or system that needs it.
cards.explanation: To “submit” work is to formally hand it in for review, approval, or use.
cards.example: The team submitted its final report online.

cards.front: What does “tidy up” mean in “I tidy up my desk before leaving”?
cards.answer: Make a place clean and organized.
cards.explanation: To “tidy up” is to put things in order and remove unnecessary mess.
cards.example: We tidied up the kitchen after dinner.

cards.front: What does “do the laundry” mean in “I do the laundry on Wednesday”?
cards.answer: Wash and usually dry clothes and other washable items.
cards.explanation: “Do the laundry” refers to the routine of cleaning clothes, towels, or similar items.
cards.example: Kai did the laundry while working from home.

cards.front: What does “go to bed” mean in “I usually go to bed before eleven”?
cards.answer: Get into bed with the intention of sleeping.
cards.explanation: To “go to bed” means to end your waking activities and prepare to sleep.
cards.example: She went to bed after reading for a few minutes.
